 Miscues adding up as CU Buffs men’s basketball hosts Portland 
 Buffaloes coming off season-high 22 turnovers against Providence

 Colorado Buffaloes guard Barrington Hargress, right, looks to pass while covered by San Diego Toreros guard Davion Hill, left, at the CU Events Center on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026. (Matthew Jonas/Staff Photographer) 
 By Pat Rooney | prooney@prairiemountainmedia.com | BuffZone PUBLISHED: November 17, 2026 at 5:24 PM MST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... The book already is out on the Colorado men’s basketball team.
 Pressure the Buffaloes, and CU gets sloppy. The turnover-prone kind of sloppy that makes every game an uphill climb.
 That’s what happened during Saturday’s loss at Providence, but it wasn’t the only time it’s happened so far this season. It’s a growing trend the Buffs will look to reverse when they host Portland at the CU Events Center on Wednesday night.
 “We have to have more pride. As a passer, as a catcher, as a cutter. You’ve got to be able to get open for your teammates,” CU head coach Tad Boyle said. “There’s a lot of things that go into it.
 “It was an issue against Marquette (in a scrimmage) and Marquette pressured us. It was an issue against North Texas, and North Texas pressured us. It was not an issue against St. Mary’s. St. Mary’s didn’t pressure us. It was an issue against San Diego State, they pressured us. What I’m getting at is, when we get pressured, it’s an issue. We’ve got to be able to handle pressure better.”
 Last year, CU averaged just 10.4 turnovers per game, the lowest mark in Boyle’s 16 full seasons with the Buffs. With Barrington Hargress posting a team-record assist-to-turnover rate of 3.61, CU averaged only 10.5 turnovers in Big 12 play, the fifth-lowest mark in the league. It’s been a different story so far this season.
 Hargress’ turnover rate is up slightly — he averaged 1.2 turnovers per game last year, and has committed 2.0 per game through CU’s 2-2 start. But he still owns an assist-to-turnover rate of 2.25, and Hargress and fellow guard Alex Dickeson (14 assists, seven turnovers) are the only rotation players with more assists than turnovers. CU has increased its turnover total in each of its first four games, culminating with 22 during Saturday’s loss at Providence.
 Friars guard Miles Byrd made history at the Buffs’ expense, as his 10 steals set a record for a CU opponent. CU goes into the Portland matchup averaging 14.8 turnovers per game.
 “Obviously Byrd was disruptive in the lanes,” Boyle said. “We knew that going into the game. I don’t think we really respected it like we should have.”

 Boyle has used a different starting lineup in all four games, yet the Buffs still haven’t put together a strong first half this season. In the opener, Abilene Christian briefly led late in the first half before CU dominated after halftime. CU trailed by 18 at halftime of a loss at San Diego State and trailed San Diego by three points at halftime before rallying for a home win.
 At Providence, the Buffs actually jumped to a 5-0 lead and still led nearly 7 minutes into the game, but by halftime the Buffs had 15 turnovers and an eight-point deficit.
 “I just feel like we’ve got to come out with a better mentality,” CU second-year wing Ian Inman said. “I feel like sometimes we get off to a slow start and then people get scared to do something. Forget get that. We’ve need to come out with energy on defense, rebound and get out and run. Our best offense is when we’re in transition and we get open shots, open layups and stuff like that. So it starts on our defensive end for sure, and I feel like we just need to throw the first punch.”
 Portland Pilots at CU Buffs men’s basketball
 TIPOFF : Wednesday, 7 p.m., CU Events Center.
 TV/RADIO : ESPN+/KOA 850 AM and 94.1 FM.
 RECORDS : Portland 3-2; Colorado 2-2.
 COACHES : Portland — Shantay Legans, 6th season (75-96, 150-145 overall). Colorado — Tad Boyle, 17th season (331-222, 387-288 overall).
 KEY PLAYERS : Portland — F James O’Donnell, 6-10, 3rd season (18.0 ppg, 10.0 rpg, .708 FG%); G Jaxon Olvera, 6-5, 4th year (14.2 ppg, 3.8 rpg, 2.8 apg, .489 FG%); G Riley Parker, 6-2, 4th year (13.0 ppg, 3.0 rpg, 3.6 apg, .526 FG%); G RJ Nance Jr., 6-2, 3rd year (11.4 ppg, 3.4 rpg, .541 FG%); G Hunter Adam, 6-7, 4th year (10.6 ppg, 4.8 rpg, .636 FG%); F Timo George, 6-8, 2nd year (10.6 ppg, 4.8 rpg, .733 FG%). Colorado — G Barrington Hargress, 6-0, 5th year (19.5 ppg, 4.5 apg, 12-for-24 3-pointers); G/F Ian Inman, 6-6, 2nd year (12.0 ppg, 3.0 rpg, 14-for-28 3-pointers); G Jalin Holland, 6-5, 2nd year (10.5 ppg, 3.0 rpg, .514 FG%);G Josiah Sanders, 6-5, 2nd year (9.3 ppg, 4.0 rpg, .423 FG%); F Justin Neely, 6-6, 5th year (6.8 ppg, 5.3 rpg); C Noah Feddersen, 6-10, 5th year (6.8 ppg, 5.8 rpg); G Alex Dickeson, 6-4, 1st year (5.8 ppg, 5.8 rpg, 3.5 apg).
 NOTES : The Buffs have won all three matchups against Portland, most recently posting a 98-69 win at home on Nov. 28, 2018. … Portland is coming off a double-overtime loss at home against East Texas A&M, a team that opened the season with a win at Oklahoma. … The Buffs held their two previous home opponents to a combined .286 mark (12-for-42) on 3-pointers. … Portland is averaging 101.8 points per game while shooting .569  from the field. … Feddersen has recorded five assists out of the post over the past two games after going without one through the first two games. … Since going 6-for-8 in the season opener, Neely has shot 2-for-12 in the past three games. … CU plays its next two games at the Acrisure Series in Palm Desert, California, beginning way from home, beginning Tuesday, Nov. 24, against Stanford. The Buffs will play either St. Louis or Grand Canyon the following day.
